claims.text: Neonates w severe cyanosis: PGE1 infusion (start 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min IV) opens the ductus arteriosus and ↑pulmonary blood flow.
claims.quote: Neonates with severe cyanosis may be palliated with an infusion of prostaglandin E1 (beginning at 0.05 to 0.1 mcg/kg/minute IV) to open the ductus arteriosus and thereby increase pulmonary blood flow.

claims.text: Hypercyanotic spell that persists after positioning, O2 and IV fluids: morphine, phenylephrine and BBs (propranolol or esmolol).
claims.quote: If the spell persists, standard medical therapy includes morphine, phenylephrine, and beta-blockers (propranolol or esmolol)
claims.locator: Treatment of Tetralogy of Fallot › Hypercyanotic spells

claims.text: Propranolol 0.25–1 mg/kg PO q6h until surgical repair may prevent recurrences.
claims.quote: Propranolol 0.25 to 1 mg/kg orally every 6 hours (given until surgical repair) may prevent recurrences.
claims.locator: Treatment of Tetralogy of Fallot › Hypercyanotic spells

claims.text: Endocarditis prophylaxis: preop, then only for the first 6 mo after repair unless a residual defect sits next to a surgical patch or prosthetic material.
claims.quote: Endocarditis prophylaxis is recommended preoperatively but is required only for the first 6 months after repair unless there is a residual defect adjacent to a surgical patch or prosthetic material.
claims.locator: Treatment of Tetralogy of Fallot › Definitive management
